content.intro: This lesson covers Ownership and Function Arguments. It sits in Module 6, Ownership and Borrowing, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Ownership and Function Arguments matters when you work with value ownership and reference validity. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Rust assigns each value an owner. Moving a non-Copy value transfers that ownership; borrowing lets code use a value temporarily without taking it over.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Ownership and Function Arguments, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops.
